standard.title: Structured oral and multimodal presentations
standard.description: plan, create, rehearse and deliver structured oral and/or multimodal presentations to report on a topic, tell a story, recount events or present an argument using subjective and objective language, complex sentences, visual features, tone, pace, pitch and volume
standard.prior_knowledge: Students plan, create and deliver presentations using clear structure, elaborated details and precise vocabulary (AC9E3LY07). They have not yet planned, rehearsed and delivered structured presentations using subjective/objective language, complex sentences and deliberate voice features.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can plan, create, rehearse and deliver structured oral and/or multimodal presentations for a range of purposes — report, story, recount, argument — using appropriate language register, complex sentences, visual features and deliberate voice control.

nodes.label: Planning the presentation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan a structured presentation by selecting appropriate structure, language register (subjective or objective) and key visual features for the purpose.
nodes.minimum_width: Plan a presentation that identifies structure, notes whether subjective or objective language is appropriate and lists at least one visual feature to include.
nodes.typical_width: Plan presentations across a range of purposes — report (objective), argument (subjective), recount (narrative past) — selecting appropriate structure, language register and visual features for each, with notes for key points rather than a script.
wider: Plan a multimodal presentation that combines spoken language with slides, images or props, and explain how visual and verbal elements complement each other
Plan a presentation for a specific audience (e.g. school assembly, parent information night) and explain how audience shapes planning choices
nodes.hinge_reason: Rehearsing in N2 requires a structured presentation to practise — voice feedback cannot be applied to language and structural choices that haven't yet been made.

response_modes.reason: Planning across presentation purposes requires explicit reasoning about register, structure and visual feature choices — the decision between objective/subjective language and appropriate structure is not intuitive without a scaffold.

success_criteria: Plan identifies the presentation's structure and purpose
Plan notes whether subjective or objective language is appropriate and gives a reason

nodes.label: Rehearsing — voice features and feedback
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can rehearse a presentation with a peer, receiving and applying feedback about tone, pace, pitch and volume.
nodes.minimum_width: Rehearse a presentation with a peer and make at least one change to tone, pace, pitch or volume based on feedback.
nodes.typical_width: Rehearse presentations with explicit attention to all four voice features — tone, pace, pitch, volume — receiving peer feedback using specific criteria and making adjustments to voice and language choices before delivery.
wider: Rehearse a presentation multiple times, tracking changes made after each rehearsal and evaluating which changes had the most impact on the presentation's effectiveness
Compare rehearsal feedback from a peer with self-evaluation using a recording and discuss where perceptions differ
nodes.hinge_reason: Delivery in N3 requires the voice features — tone, pace, pitch, volume — to have been practised and adjusted in N2 — unrehearsed delivery cannot demonstrate deliberate voice control.

response_modes.reason: Voice feature control — using pace, pitch, volume and tone deliberately — is a performance skill that requires repeated rehearsal across multiple contexts to become reliably available.

success_criteria: Has rehearsed with a peer and can name one piece of specific voice feedback received
Has made at least one change to delivery based on feedback

nodes.label: Delivering the presentation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can deliver a structured presentation using appropriate language, complex sentences, visual features and deliberate voice control for the purpose and audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Deliver a structured presentation on a topic using at least one complex sentence and at least one deliberate voice feature (e.g. slowing pace for emphasis).
nodes.typical_width: Deliver presentations across a range of purposes — report, argument, recount — with appropriate language register, complex sentences, integrated visual features and deliberate voice control (tone, pace, pitch, volume) suited to purpose and audience.
wider: Deliver the same content in two different presentation contexts (e.g. formal classroom vs informal small group) and reflect on how delivery changes across contexts
Deliver a presentation incorporating First Nations Australian content with attention to respectful language choices and appropriate acknowledgement conventions

response_modes.reason: Delivering a presentation integrates planning, language knowledge and rehearsed voice control into a single live performance — the full capability of the descriptor.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of purposes, audiences and formats for structured presentation is genuinely wide — report, argument, recount, multimodal — producing rich variation in delivery choices.
success_criteria: Presentation has a clear structure with introduction and conclusion
At least one complex sentence is used in delivery
At least one deliberate voice feature is evident — pace, volume, pitch or tone varied for effect
